title: Build-context overlay in v1.44 makes using buildah in container harder
body:
### Issue Description

We use buildah containerized (in a Kubernetes Pod, via Tekton) with native overlay. Up to and including v1.43.1, this only required mounting a host directory over `/var/lib/containers/storage` or the equivalent rootless path (assuming the host directory is on a filesystem that supports overlay).

Version 1.44 adds an overlay over the build context directory and puts the `upper` and `work` directories to `/var/tmp` by default, which creates another obstacle for containerized usage (perhaps unnecessarily?).

Workarounds:
1. Mount a host dir over `/var/tmp` as well
2. Set `engine.image_copy_tmp_dir = "/var/lib/containers/storage"` (or equivalent rootless path) in `containers.conf`

Looks like a good workaround but doesn't work:
1. Set `engine.image_copy_tmp_dir = "storage"` in `containers.conf`
    - this makes buildah attempt to put the overlay under `<containers storage path>/tmp`, but fails with `Error: mounting an overlay over build context directory: creating temporary directory: stat /var/lib/containers/storage/tmp: no such file or directory`

### Steps to reproduce the issue

Steps to reproduce the issue

1. Create a Containerfile for installing buildah + dependencies:

    ```Dockerfile
    FROM registry.access.redhat.com/ubi10/go-toolset:1.26.3 AS go-build

    ARG BUILDAH_TAG=v1.44.0

    USER 0

    # Install dependencies for compiling buildah
    RUN dnf -y install \
            bzip2 \
            glib2-devel \
            gpgme-devel \
            libassuan-devel \
            libseccomp-devel

    WORKDIR /build

    RUN git clone --branch=$BUILDAH_TAG https://github.com/podman-container-tools/buildah && \
        cd buildah && \
        make bin/buildah


    FROM registry.access.redhat.com/ubi10/ubi-minimal:10.1

    USER 0

    RUN microdnf -y install \
            containers-common-extra \
            gpgme \
            libassuan \
            libseccomp

    COPY --from=go-build /build/buildah/bin/buildah /usr/local/bin/buildah

    COPY <<EOF /etc/containers/storage.conf
    [storage]
    driver = "overlay"
    EOF

    ENV BUILDAH_ISOLATION=chroot
    ```

2. Build it: `buildah build -t buildah:1.44.0 .`
3. Try to run a build:

    ```bash
    podman run --rm -i -v /var/lib/containers/storage buildah:1.44.0 bash <<EOF
    mkdir /tmp/buildcontext
    cd /tmp/buildcontext
    echo 'FROM scratch' > Containerfile
    buildah build
    EOF
    ```

    ```text
    Error: mounting an overlay over build context directory: creating overlay scaffolding for build context directory: mount overlay:/var/tmp/buildah-context-855737399/overlay/890669428/merge, data: lowerdir=/tmp/buildcontext,upperdir=/var/tmp/buildah-context-855737399/overlay/890669428/upper,workdir=/var/tmp/buildah-context-855737399/overlay/890669428/work,userxattr: invalid argument
    ```

4. Try again with `image_copy_tmp_dir = "storage"`:

    ```bash
    podman run --rm -i -v /var/lib/containers/storage buildah:1.44.0 bash <<EOF
    mkdir /tmp/buildcontext
    cd /tmp/buildcontext
    echo 'FROM scratch' > Containerfile

    mkdir /etc/containers/containers.conf.d
    printf '[engine]\nimage_copy_tmp_dir = "storage"' >/etc/containers/containers.conf.d/set-tmp-dir.conf

    buildah build
    EOF
    ```

    ```text
    Error: mounting an overlay over build context directory: creating temporary directory: stat /var/lib/containers/storage/tmp: no such file or directory
    ```

### Describe the results you received

Containerized usage now requires a non-obvious volume mount or configuration change

### Describe the results you expected

Ideally, expected the build context overlay to be created in the container storage dir by default and just work.
Alternatively, expected the `engine.image_copy_tmp_dir = "storage"` setting to solve the problem.

comments.body:
We're hitting the same problem with `STORAGE_DRIVER=vfs` and `BUILDAH_ISOLATION=chroot` in a GitLab CI runner (Kubernetes executor).

Our setup uses a custom image based on Wolfi with buildah, where we build OCI images inside the CI job. With v1.44, the unconditional overlay mount over the build context fails even though we explicitly use the `vfs` storage driver:

```
Error: mounting an overlay over build context directory: creating overlay scaffolding for build context directory: mount overlay:/var/tmp/buildah-context-852256633/overlay/377000136/merge, data: lowerdir=/builds/...,upperdir=/var/tmp/buildah-context-852256633/overlay/377000136/upper,workdir=/var/tmp/buildah-context-852256633/overlay/377000136/work: invalid argument
```

The build context overlay appears to bypass the storage driver setting entirely - setting `STORAGE_DRIVER=vfs`, passing `--storage-driver vfs` on the CLI, or pointing `CONTAINERS_STORAGE_CONF` to a custom config with `driver = "vfs"` all have no effect. The overlay mount is attempted regardless.

We had to pin buildah to 1.43.1 as a workaround. It would be great if the build context overlay either respected the configured storage driver or had a fallback/opt-out when the overlay mount fails.

Another issue I found with this overlay mount is that it is not marked as volatile (does not have [volatile](https://www.redhat.com/en/blog/container-volatile-overlay-mounts) mount option). Thus, unmount of this overlay on a busy CI host is taking really long time.

I was able to workaround the problem; however, I don't like it too much.

```
  before_script:
    - mkdir -p "$CI_PROJECT_DIR/.buildah-tmp"
    - export TMPDIR="$CI_PROJECT_DIR/.buildah-tmp"
```
same error here with gitlab kubernetes executor. Workaround helps but not optimal

Same problem here.
On our case is on a github self-hosted runner, on k8s mode. With an wolfi based image, with buildah configured with VFS and chroot isolation.

We do not tested the workaround yet; we prefer stay at 1.43.1 that works flawlessly  with the setup. But please fix, or add a flag to keep the old behavior on buildah for these cases.

Thanks :-)
A friendly reminder that this issue had no activity for 30 days.
I think this is still relevant. Unfortunately, haven't had a chance to test v1.44.1 or v1.45.0 if it's fixed there.

> Unfortunately, haven't had a chance to test v1.44.1 or v1.45.0 if it's fixed there.

Just tried the reproducer with BUILDAH_TAG=v1.45.0, the behavior looks the same. So yes, still relevant

> this only required mounting a host directory over `/var/lib/containers/storage`

I think that was because it wrote to `/var/lib/containers/storage`, and now it does so to `/var/tmp`.

Taking your example, adding this to the build image fixes it for me, no other change to the pipeline needed:

```Containerfile
(...)
FROM registry.access.redhat.com/ubi10/ubi-minimal:10.1
VOLUME /var/tmp
(...)
```

I had a `VOLUME /var/lib/containers` before, just switched it to `/var/tmp`.

~~EDIT: I was wrong about `/var/lib/containers`, the `VOLUME` is still needed if building without fuse-overlayfs.~~

EDIT2: buildah strips the SYS_ADMIN permissions needed to work with the native overlay driver, or keep `VOLUME /var/lib/containers/`in the build image. So for me, moving the volume mount from /var/lib/containers to /var/tmp fixed my pipeline, but I can't get rid of fuse-overlayfs in the image without switching to vfs.
This is still relevant

Still relevant, not stale

A quick fix is for this within containers is to run:
```console
$ sed 's/^#mount_program/mount_program/g' /usr/share/containers/storage.conf >/etc/containers/storage.conf
```
This is the same what `quay.io/buildah/stable` does ([here](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/image_build/blob/b86020d8c306c4724780adfb6fc492d0a2d9cc48/buildah/Containerfile#L84)) which replaces the default `mount` call with the `fuse-overlayfs` command.
This is still broken in 1.45.1.
The `v1` tag on Quay has been updated to v1.45.1 from 1.43.5 and this is now affecting a lot more people.
I can confirm that a build pipeline working yesterday is now failing. After downgrading to v1.43, everything works fine again.

I can not confirm. I was typing to warn about the tag moving to a newer version on quay, but tested it (it worked fine) and instead wrote the workaround. Now with the new tag I reran a pipeline job and it worked as before. So the new version with its patched `storage.conf` is working just fine. The tag the job used is `v1` (`quay.io/buildah/stable@sha256:2807c70ecb10a9352e016eacaa2e1d5e8ab1ebe8c36313641727f87531f25b50`) and the runner is a fedora bootc image daily build based on `quay.io/fedora/fedora-bootc:latest` with a `dnf` installed `podman` (6.1.3) and the job runs with a passed `/dev/fuse` device, non-privileged, and `seccomp:unconfined`.

We're using buildah through the Kubernetes executor for Gitlab CI, and its containers run as unprivileged. The underlying runtime is containerd. I can confirm the workaround is needed.

Yes, the workaround is definitely needed, but the `quay.io/buildah/stable` image includes it for quite a while. So at least for me I do not need to change anything, but I am redeploying a worker with docker to check if it is a problem there. Using the binary by itself though is another story and there the workaround must be added manually.

No, I've no GitLab Runner using podman available. But I've just reproduced the issue using the GitLab Runner on Docker 24.0.7-ce.
We're running on OpenShift using BuildConfig with a custom image that contains the buildah binary. Have to pin buildah on last version of 1.43

I've deployed a docker runner in the mean time and the job still runs. Docker version 29.9.2, build 2.fc45 (`moby-engine` from Fedora repos) and the rest is the same as with the podman runner setup. I am not sure why it works on my machine, but not yours ^^ . I only get the error when I use a plain Fedora image for the job and install buildah via dnf and thus without the workaround. As soon as I add the workaround to such a job, I works. Really odd :/

Here using Gitlab Runner with Docker, launching a custom docker image (alpine 3.24 + buildah).
When buildah 1.44 appeared in alpine repos, I had to do the workaround with the volume :
```
FROM alpine:3.24

RUN apk add --no-cache buildah netavark fuse-overlayfs

VOLUME /var/tmp
```

Ok just to make sure, I talk about `quay.io/buildah/stable` (working for me) vs any other install method (be it a alpine container and installing with `apk` or fedora container and installing with `dnf` or whatsoever). Most of the later (probably) or even all do not have such a workaround like with the `mount_program`. These are "expected" to fail, but `quay.io/buildah/stable` should still work (at least it does for me) or adding one of the workarounds mentioned in this thread.
